This notebook is a single paper-facing map for the PNAS draft.
It is ordered like the paper, uses the saved `Datasets/` objects whenever possible, and keeps the raw-data refresh optional.

## How to use

- Render as a concise map only: keep all parameters at `FALSE`.
- Rebuild the paper assets from saved objects: set `run_saved_build = TRUE`.
- Refresh the saved datasets first: set both `run_raw_refresh = TRUE` and `run_saved_build = TRUE`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
repo_root <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

if (exists("params") && is.list(params)) {
  run_saved_build <- isTRUE(params$run_saved_build)
  run_raw_refresh <- isTRUE(params$run_raw_refresh)
} else {
  run_saved_build <- FALSE
  run_raw_refresh <- FALSE
}

assert_required_packages <- function(packages, context) {
  missing <- packages[!vapply(packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "[", context, "] Missing required R packages:\n- ",
        paste(sort(unique(missing)), collapse = "\n- "),
        "\n\nInstall the missing packages listed in README.md, then rerun PAPER_REPRODUCTION.Rmd."
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
}

required_notebook_packages <- c("knitr", "rmarkdown")
required_build_packages <- c(
  "here", "rmarkdown", "signal",
  "tidyverse", "cowplot", "ggpubr", "extrafont", "readxl", "writexl",
  "ggfittext", "ggridges", "ggrepel", "knitr", "waterfalls", "ggforce",
  "ggdist", "directlabels", "gganimate", "gifski", "png", "kableExtra",
  "stargazer", "zoo", "data.table", "purrr", "xtable", "readODS",
  "viridis", "scales", "broom", "Polychrome", "RColorBrewer", "ggpattern",
  "ggview", "tidytext", "patchwork", "car", "lmtest", "sandwich", "nlme"
)

assert_required_packages(required_notebook_packages, "PAPER_REPRODUCTION setup")

if (run_saved_build || run_raw_refresh) {
  assert_required_packages(
    unique(c(required_notebook_packages, required_build_packages)),
    "PAPER_REPRODUCTION build mode"
  )
}

source_script <- function(path) {
  source(file.path(repo_root, path), local = new.env(parent = globalenv()))
}

render_notebook <- function(path) {
  rmarkdown::render(
    input = file.path(repo_root, path),
    quiet = TRUE,
    clean = TRUE,
    envir = new.env(parent = globalenv())
  )
}

build_flags <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

run_saved_step <- function(key, fun) {
  if (!isTRUE(run_saved_build)) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if (!exists(key, envir = build_flags, inherits = FALSE)) {
    fun()
    assign(key, TRUE, envir = build_flags)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

run_raw_step <- function(key, fun) {
  if (!isTRUE(run_raw_refresh)) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if (!exists(key, envir = build_flags, inherits = FALSE)) {
    fun()
    assign(key, TRUE, envir = build_flags)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

show_saved_figure <- function(path, preview_path = path, title = NULL) {
  preview_file <- file.path(repo_root, preview_path)
  preview_rel <- gsub("\\\\", "/", preview_path)
  saved_rel <- gsub("\\\\", "/", path)
  figure_name <- basename(path)
  preview_ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(preview_path))
  preview_dir <- dirname(preview_path)
  preview_base <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(preview_path))

  cat(sprintf("Saved figure: `%s`\n\n", figure_name))
  cat(sprintf("Location: `%s`\n\n", saved_rel))

  if (!is.null(title) && nzchar(title)) {
    cat(sprintf("Context: %s\n\n", title))
  }

  if (file.exists(preview_file)) {
    if (identical(preview_ext, "pdf")) {
      image_candidates <- file.path(
        preview_dir,
        paste0(preview_base, c(".svg", ".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg"))
      )
      image_candidate <- image_candidates[file.exists(file.path(repo_root, image_candidates))][1]

      if (!is.na(image_candidate)) {
        image_rel <- gsub("\\\\", "/", image_candidate)
        cat(sprintf("![%s](%s)\n\n", figure_name, image_rel))
      } else {
        cat(sprintf("Preview: PDF asset, open [%s](%s).\n\n", figure_name, preview_rel))
      }
    } else {
      cat(sprintf("![%s](%s)\n\n", figure_name, preview_rel))
    }
  } else {
    cat("_Figure not found yet. Run the corresponding build step._\n\n")
  }
}

tex_row_parts <- function(row) {
  trimws(strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "", row), " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
}

find_tex_parts <- function(lines, pattern, fixed = TRUE) {
  row <- trimws(lines[grepl(pattern, lines, fixed = fixed)][1])
  tex_row_parts(row)
}

signed_label <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  sprintf(paste0("%+.", digits, "f"), x)
}
```

## Main text

Headline numbers repeated in the abstract, introduction, and discussion:

- UK CCC economy-wide scenarios by 2050: `-1.3` to `+0.1` pp.
- Global fast-transition energy scenario: about `5.8%` aggregate TFP by 2050, or nearly `6` percentage points in the prose.
- Same period for the scenario applications: `2022--2050`.

### Figure 1

This is the main framework figure in `2_results_method.tex`.
It introduces the scenario -> sectoral TFP -> Domar aggregation -> aggregate TFP pipeline and provides the validation panels used in the paper.

Key number to match in the text: baseline zeta = `r zeta_fig1_label`.

```{r fig1-build, eval=run_saved_build}
run_saved_step("fig1", function() {
  source_script("Schema/0_plot_schematic.R")
})
```

Repo output:

- `Schema/figure1_framework_validation.pdf`

```{r fig1-show, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
)
```

### Cement example

This is the static robustness table embedded in `3-results-CCC.tex`.
It illustrates why a large shock in a small sector can have a tiny aggregate effect.

Text numbers to match:

- Cement Domar weight in the UK: `0.003`.
- Annualisation divisor for the 2022--2050 cumulative effect: `28`.
- Stress tests: cost shock `240%`, quantity growth `100%`, and Domar weight `0.006`.
- With a `1%` baseline annual TFP growth rate, the cement transition leaves annual growth between `0.986%` and `0.999%`.
- The headline aggregate effect is less than `0.2` percentage points in the introduction; the table's extreme cost-shock row is `-0.21%`.
- Cement table rows: IEA cost `60%--110%`, sector TFP `-48%` to `-34%`, aggregate `-0.13%` to `-0.08%`, annual `-0.004` to `-0.003` %/yr.
- Cement table rows: MPP cost `40%--120%`, sector TFP `-50%` to `-25%`, aggregate `-0.14%` to `-0.06%`, annual `-0.005` to `-0.002` %/yr.
- Cement table rows: McKinsey cost `45%`, sector TFP `-28%`, aggregate `-0.06%`, annual `-0.002` %/yr.
- Cement stress rows: higher cost sector TFP `-66%`, annual `-0.007` %/yr; output-doubles aggregate `-0.4%` to `-0.12%`; higher-Domar aggregate `-0.41%` to `-0.18%`.

### CCC main results

This block feeds `3-results-CCC.tex`.

Key numbers to match in the text:

- CB7 about `r cb7_2050_pp_label` pp by 2050.
- CB6 about `r cb6_best_2050_pp_label` to `r cb6_worst_2050_pp_label` pp by 2050.
- Annual effect about `r ccc_annual_effect_min_label`-`r ccc_annual_effect_max_label` pp/year.
- Residential buildings can contribute about `r residential_min_pp_label` pp.
- CCC scope: `14` sectors and `6` scenarios, with CB6 covering `2033--2037` and CB7 covering `2038--2042`.
- Main figure scope: one CB7 Balanced Pathway scenario and `5` CB6 scenarios; CB7 vintage `2025`, CB6 vintage `2020`; shaded bands are `90%` empirical prediction intervals.
- Annual-growth translation in the prose: a `1%` baseline annual TFP rate becomes `0.96%` to `1.003%`; US measurement-error comparison is about `0.2` pp/year over `2005--2015`.
- CB7 uses the Green Book `3.5%` rate for social discounting; the financing sensitivity moves the CB7 aggregate effect from `r cb7_finance_base_label` pp to `r cb7_finance_greenbook_label` pp at discount-rate `0.035`, and to `r cb7_finance_private_label` pp at discount-rate `0.15`.
- CCC uncertainty propagation uses covered-sector Domar weight `r ccc_domar_sum_label` and whole-economy scaling ratio `r ccc_domar_scale_label`.
- Quantity-growth sensitivity: OBR growth `r quantity_growth_obr_label` implies `r quantity_growth_sector_label` pp at sector level and about `r quantity_growth_aggregate_label` pp after scaling by a `0.5` combined Domar weight.

```{r energy-key-numbers, include=FALSE}
energy_main_uk_bnz_price_label <- energy_uk_bnz_breakdown_parts[2]
energy_main_uk_bnz_output_label <- energy_uk_bnz_breakdown_parts[3]

energy_summary_lines <- readLines(
  file.path(repo_root, "Tables/Energy/tab_summary_energy_tfp_scenarios.tex"),
  warn = FALSE
)

energy_appendix_ccc_rows <- trimws(energy_summary_lines[grepl("CCC CB6 ", energy_summary_lines, fixed = TRUE)])
energy_appendix_ccc_parts <- lapply(
  energy_appendix_ccc_rows,
  function(x) trimws(strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "", x), " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
)
energy_appendix_ccc_energy_vals <- as.numeric(gsub("%", "", vapply(energy_appendix_ccc_parts, `[`, "", 5), fixed = TRUE))
energy_appendix_ccc_agg_vals <- as.numeric(gsub("%", "", vapply(energy_appendix_ccc_parts, `[`, "", 6), fixed = TRUE))
energy_appendix_ccc_energy_min_label <- paste0(format(min(energy_appendix_ccc_energy_vals), trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), "%")
energy_appendix_ccc_energy_max_label <- paste0(format(max(energy_appendix_ccc_energy_vals), trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), "%")
energy_appendix_ccc_agg_min_label <- paste0(format(min(energy_appendix_ccc_agg_vals), trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), "%")
energy_appendix_ccc_agg_max_label <- paste0(format(max(energy_appendix_ccc_agg_vals), trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), "%")

energy_appendix_ccc_bnz_parts <- energy_appendix_ccc_parts[
  grepl("Balanced Net Zero Pathway", vapply(energy_appendix_ccc_parts, `[`, "", 1), fixed = TRUE)
][[1]]
energy_appendix_ccc_bnz_tfp_label <- energy_appendix_ccc_bnz_parts[5]
energy_appendix_ccc_bnz_agg_label <- energy_appendix_ccc_bnz_parts[6]

energy_appendix_world_no_transition_row <- trimws(
  energy_summary_lines[grepl("World No Transition & BEIS + Way & 7 &", energy_summary_lines, fixed = TRUE)][1]
)
energy_appendix_world_no_transition_parts <- trimws(
  strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "", energy_appendix_world_no_transition_row), " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
)
energy_appendix_world_no_transition_tfp_label <- energy_appendix_world_no_transition_parts[5]
energy_appendix_world_no_transition_agg_label <- energy_appendix_world_no_transition_parts[6]

energy_appendix_world_all_way_row <- trimws(
  energy_summary_lines[grepl("World Fast Transition & All Way & 7 &", energy_summary_lines, fixed = TRUE)][1]
)
energy_appendix_world_all_way_parts <- trimws(
  strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "", energy_appendix_world_all_way_row), " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
)
energy_appendix_world_all_way_tfp_label <- energy_appendix_world_all_way_parts[5]
energy_appendix_world_all_way_agg_label <- energy_appendix_world_all_way_parts[6]

energy_overgeneration_lines <- readLines(
  file.path(repo_root, "Tables/Energy/tab_main_overgeneration_sensitivity.tex"),
  warn = FALSE
)
energy_appendix_world_no_over_row <- trimws(
  energy_overgeneration_lines[grepl("No overproduction & 1.00 & World Fast Transition", energy_overgeneration_lines, fixed = TRUE)][1]
)
energy_appendix_world_no_over_parts <- trimws(
  strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "", energy_appendix_world_no_over_row), " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
)
energy_appendix_world_no_over_tfp_label <- energy_appendix_world_no_over_parts[5]
energy_appendix_world_no_over_agg_label <- energy_appendix_world_no_over_parts[6]

energy_appendix_world_baseline_row <- trimws(
  energy_overgeneration_lines[grepl("Current baseline & 1.50 & World Fast Transition", energy_overgeneration_lines, fixed = TRUE)][1]
)
energy_appendix_world_baseline_parts <- trimws(
  strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "", energy_appendix_world_baseline_row), " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
)
energy_appendix_world_baseline_tfp_label <- energy_appendix_world_baseline_parts[5]
energy_appendix_world_baseline_agg_label <- energy_appendix_world_baseline_parts[6]

energy_logbp_to_pct <- function(x) 100 * (exp(x / 10000) - 1)
energy_gap_initial_price_label <- sprintf("%.1f", energy_logbp_to_pct(energy_text_numbers$uk_world_useful_initial_price_logbp))
energy_gap_quantity_label <- sprintf("%.1f", energy_logbp_to_pct(energy_text_numbers$uk_world_useful_quantity_logbp))
energy_gap_mix_label <- sprintf("%.1f", energy_logbp_to_pct(energy_text_numbers$uk_world_useful_mix_logbp))
energy_solar_shift_label <- sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * energy_text_numbers$solar_shift_to_wind_share)

final_energy_uk_fast_pp <- final_energy_tfp_scenarios$cum_hat_pp[
  final_energy_tfp_scenarios$Scenario_q == "UK fast transition"
][1]
final_energy_world_fast_pp <- final_energy_tfp_scenarios$cum_hat_pp[
  final_energy_tfp_scenarios$Scenario_q == "Fast_Transition"
][1]
final_energy_uk_fast_label <- sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * final_energy_uk_fast_pp)
final_energy_world_fast_label <- sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * final_energy_world_fast_pp)

way_all_cost_2022 <- df_total_cost_compare_way$cost_trillion_usd[
  df_total_cost_compare_way$Scenario_q == "Fast_Transition" &
    df_total_cost_compare_way$Year == 2022 &
    df_total_cost_compare_way$price_source == "All Way"
][1]
way_all_cost_2050 <- df_total_cost_compare_way$cost_trillion_usd[
  df_total_cost_compare_way$Scenario_q == "Fast_Transition" &
    df_total_cost_compare_way$Year == 2050 &
    df_total_cost_compare_way$price_source == "All Way"
][1]
way_no_over_cost_2022 <- df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$cost_trillion_usd[
  df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$Scenario_q == "Fast_Transition" &
    df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$Year == 2022 &
    df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$price_source == "All Way"
][1]
way_no_over_cost_2050 <- df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$cost_trillion_usd[
  df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$Scenario_q == "Fast_Transition" &
    df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$Year == 2050 &
    df_total_cost_compare_way_no_overgeneration$price_source == "All Way"
][1]
way_all_cost_2022_label <- sprintf("%.2f", way_all_cost_2022)
way_all_cost_2050_label <- sprintf("%.2f", way_all_cost_2050)
way_no_over_cost_2022_label <- sprintf("%.2f", way_no_over_cost_2022)
way_no_over_cost_2050_label <- sprintf("%.2f", way_no_over_cost_2050)
way_overgeneration_cost_share_label <- sprintf(
  "%.0f%%",
  100 * (way_all_cost_2050 - way_no_over_cost_2050) / way_all_cost_2050
)
```

### Energy main results

This block feeds `4-results-energy.tex`.
It is the main-text energy application: the world fast transition, the UK fast-transition counterfactual, and the UK CCC pathway, plus the main decomposition table.

Key numbers to match in the text:

- World fast transition: `r energy_main_world_tfp_label` energy TFP, `r energy_main_world_agg_label` aggregate TFP, and `r energy_main_world_annual_label` pp/year.
- UK fast transition: `r energy_main_uk_fast_tfp_label` energy TFP, `r energy_main_uk_fast_agg_label` aggregate TFP, and `r energy_main_uk_fast_annual_label` pp/year.
- UK CCC pathway: `r energy_main_uk_bnz_tfp_label` energy TFP, `r energy_main_uk_bnz_agg_label` aggregate TFP, and `r energy_main_uk_bnz_annual_label` pp/year.
- Saved decomposition table: world fast transition is `r energy_main_world_price_label` from prices and `r energy_main_world_output_label` from output, while UK Balanced Net Zero is `r energy_main_uk_bnz_price_label` from prices and `r energy_main_uk_bnz_output_label` from output.
- Energy-literature context cited before the application: aggregate real wages rising `2--3%`, and labour productivity growing `0.1%` after `5` years in referenced studies.
- UK fast-transition calculation cited in prose: `61%` energy productivity growth, Domar weight `0.024`, `ln(0.61 + 1) * 0.024 = 0.011`, hence `1.1` pp over `2022--2050` or `0.04` pp/year.
- UK CCC energy prose: about `13%` energy productivity growth, just over one fifth of a pp, `0.29` pp over `2022--2050`, or `0.01` pp/year.
- UK/world fast-transition gap decomposition: initial energy prices `r energy_gap_initial_price_label` pp, useful-energy demand growth `r energy_gap_quantity_label` pp, and solar-to-wind mix `r energy_gap_mix_label` pp.
- UK fast transition construction shifts `r energy_solar_shift_label` of the Way et al. solar quantity to wind to match UK conditions.
- CCC Balanced Net Zero mix includes abated gas and biomass equal to `4.8%` of final energy in `2050`; the Way et al. pathway has none.
- Final-energy rather than useful-energy accounting is cited in the text as `-8%` for UK fast transition and `43%` for the global fast transition.
- Energy-sector Domar weights in the figure caption: `0.067` for the world and `0.024` for the UK; calibrated `zeta = 0.13`.

### Empirical validation appendix

This block feeds `A6-Empirical_validation.tex`.
It justifies the reduced-form productivity bridge, the choice of `zeta`, and the uncertainty bands used later in the scenario exercises.

Key numbers to match in the appendix:

- Domar horizon-20 mean error `r domar_h20_mean_pp_label` pp, with 10-90 range [`r domar_h20_q10_pp_label`, `r domar_h20_q90_pp_label`] pp.
- Domar support: `18` countries in the final complete-coverage sample, `r domar_n_h20_label` observations at horizon 20, and `r domar_n_last_label` observations at the last observed horizon (`r domar_horizon_last_label`).
- Baseline zeta = `r zeta_baseline_label`.
- Compact zeta calibration table: KLEMS baseline horizons `r zeta_calib_klems_baseline_horizons_label`, `r zeta_calib_klems_baseline_obs_label` observations, zeta `r zeta_calib_klems_baseline_label`; KLEMS all horizons `r zeta_calib_klems_all_label`; STAN `r zeta_calib_stan_label`; NBER long horizon `r zeta_calib_nber_long_label`.
- KLEMS all horizons `r zeta_klems_all_label`.
- STAN `r zeta_stan_label`.
- NBER CES long horizon `r zeta_nber_long_label`.
- Horizon-`r klems_horizon_label` KLEMS additive correction median `r klems_h30_q50_label`, with 10-90 range [`r klems_h30_q10_label`, `r klems_h30_q90_label`].
- FE regression estimate `r zeta_fe_h18_no_fe_label` without fixed effects and `r zeta_fe_h18_label` with country, sector, and year fixed effects at horizon 18 (`r zeta_fe_h18_n_label` observations).
- FE regression checks cited in prose: `0.195` at horizon `15`, `0.129` at horizon `18`, `0.132` at horizon `20`, and `0.130` at horizon `23`.
- Accuracy-objective zeta robustness ranges cited in prose: KLEMS `0.119--0.150`, NBER CES `0.112--0.146`; STAN has shorter horizon support.
- Cross-sector long-horizon correlations: raw [`r corr_tfp_raw_label`, `r corr_price_raw_label`, `r corr_output_raw_label`] for TFP, real prices, and real output; demeaned [`r corr_tfp_demeaned_label`, `r corr_price_demeaned_label`, `r corr_output_demeaned_label`].
- Joint zeta-Domar calibration: long-horizon aggregate MAE zeta `r joint_zeta_long_mae_label`; unit-Domar counterfactual zeta `r unit_zeta_long_mae_label`.

### Energy appendix

This is `B2-energy.tex`.
It contains the CCC scenario range, the conversion factors, the price calibration table, the overgeneration robustness, and the alternative all-Way price figure.

Key numbers to match in the appendix:

- CCC range `r energy_appendix_ccc_energy_min_label`-`r energy_appendix_ccc_energy_max_label` energy TFP and `r energy_appendix_ccc_agg_min_label`-`r energy_appendix_ccc_agg_max_label` aggregate TFP.
- CCC Balanced Net Zero `r energy_appendix_ccc_bnz_tfp_label` energy TFP and `r energy_appendix_ccc_bnz_agg_label` aggregate TFP.
- World No Transition `r energy_appendix_world_no_transition_tfp_label` energy TFP and `r energy_appendix_world_no_transition_agg_label` aggregate TFP.
- World Fast Transition under all-Way prices `r energy_appendix_world_all_way_tfp_label` energy TFP and `r energy_appendix_world_all_way_agg_label` aggregate TFP.
- Overgeneration robustness: current baseline `r energy_appendix_world_baseline_tfp_label` and `r energy_appendix_world_baseline_agg_label`, versus no overproduction `r energy_appendix_world_no_over_tfp_label` and `r energy_appendix_world_no_over_agg_label`.
- Way all-price calibration costs: USD `r way_all_cost_2022_label` trillion in 2022 and USD `r way_all_cost_2050_label` trillion in 2050.
- Without wind/solar overgeneration, the same costs are USD `r way_no_over_cost_2022_label` trillion in 2022 and USD `r way_no_over_cost_2050_label` trillion in 2050; overgeneration is `r way_overgeneration_cost_share_label` of 2050 system costs.
- Static quantity/conversion checks cited in the text: `1` Mtoe = `11.63` TWh, `1` EJ = `277.78` TWh, UK primary energy equivalent `170` Mtoe, recovered CCC quantity `1866` TWh (about `160` Mtoe), and an implied `6%` quantity gap worth `0.8` pp of energy-industry TFP.
- Grid and storage assumptions cited in the text: hydrogen conversion efficiency `0.5`, plant-cost adder `14` USD/MWh, wind/solar overgeneration factor `1.5`, baseline grid adder `7` USD/MWh, robustness grid adders `0` and `14` USD/MWh, and battery storage capacity `30%` of generated wind-plus-solar electricity.
- Grid back-of-the-envelope cited in the text: network cost shifts UK Fast energy TFP by about `11` pp; wind is about `20` USD/MWh in 2050 and `32` with overgeneration; solar is `10.6` USD/MWh and `17` with overgeneration; the `7` USD/MWh grid adder is `21%` for wind and `40%` for solar, with `44%` and `9%` useful-energy shares, producing about a `12.5%` average-price increase and roughly `-11%` energy productivity through `(0.13 - 1) * 0.125`.
- Overgeneration text convention: producing `1` TWh of consumed electricity requires `1.5` TWh generated on average when overproduction is stored.
